source.title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let 0 < λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ··· be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian, defined by −Δu = λu in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω. Must the ratio (λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)/λ₁ always be at most the corresponding value for the Euclidean n-ball, namely n j_{p+1,1}² / j_{p,1}² where p = (n−2)/2 and j_{ν,k} denotes the k-th positive zero of the Bessel function J_ν? In particular, for n = 2, is (λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁)_disk ≈ 5.077?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² show that (λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁)|disk ≈ 5.077. In ℝⁿ this conjecture reads (λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)/λ₁ ≤ n j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1}.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues 0 < λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ ···. For every integer m ≥ 2, must λₘ₊₁/λₘ be at most the ball value j_{p+1,1}² / j_{p,1}², where p = (n−2)/2 and j_{ν,k} is the k-th positive zero of J_ν? In dimension 2, this asks whether λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)_disk ≈ 2.5387 for all m ≥ 2.

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² and all m ≥ 2 show that λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)|disk ≈ 2.5387. In ℝⁿ this conjecture reads λₘ₊₁/λₘ ≤ j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1}.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁, λ₂, .... For every integer m ≥ 1, must the even-index ratio λ₂ₘ/λₘ always satisfy λ₂ₘ/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)_{n-ball}?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ and all m ≥ 1 show that λ₂ₘ/λₘ ≤ (λ₂/λ₁)|n-ball.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω vary over bounded domains in ℝⁿ, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be its Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. For every pair of integers k, m ≥ 1, must one always have λ_{km}/λₘ ≤ sup_D λ_k(D)/λ₁(D), where the supremum is taken over bounded domains D?

evidence.quote: or even λ_{km}/λₘ ≤ sup_Ω λ_k/λ₁.

accepted.question_text: Among bounded domains Ω in ℝⁿ, what is the optimal upper bound for the Dirichlet eigenvalue ratio λ₃/λ₁, and which domain realizes that supremum, possibly only in a limiting sense? In particular, in dimension 2 the source asks for the exact value of sup_Ω λ₃/λ₁ and the optimizer, noting that the disk is not optimal.

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ find the optimal bound on λ₃/λ₁ and the shape of domain that saturates it (possibly in a limiting sense). In ℝ² it is known that 35/11 ≈ 3.1818 ≤ sup_Ω λ₃/λ₁ ≤ 3.83103.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be its Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. Must the ratio λₙ₊₂/λ₁ always be at most the corresponding ratio for the n-ball, namely j_{p+2,1}² / j_{p,1}² with p = (n−2)/2?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ show that λₙ₊₂/λ₁ ≤ (λₙ₊₂/λ₁)|n-ball = j²_{p+2,1}/j²_{p,1}.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ···. Must the next multiplicity-cluster sums also be bounded by their ball values, namely λ₄ + λ₅ over λ₁ in dimension 2 and, in general dimension n, (λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})/λ₁ ≤ ((n−1)(n+2)/2) · j_{p+2,1}² / j_{p,1}²?

evidence.quote: It may also be true that in two dimensions (λ₄ + λ₅)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₄ + λ₅)/λ₁)|disk = 2j²_{2,1}/j²_{0,1} ≈ 9.121 and in general dimension n (λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})/λ₁ ≤ ((n−1)(n+2)/2) j²_{p+2,1}/j²_{p,1}.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ···. Must the reciprocal-gap sum ∑_{i=1}^n λ₁/(λ_{i+1}−λ₁) be at least the corresponding value for the n-ball, namely n / (j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1} − 1) where p = (n−2)/2? In dimension 2 this is the inequality λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁) ≥ ((λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁))_disk) ≈ 1.2998.

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² show that λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁) ≥ ((λ₁/(λ₂−λ₁) + λ₁/(λ₃−λ₁))|disk) ≈ 1.2998 and, more generally, for Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ show that ∑_{i=1}^n λ₁/(λ_{i+1}−λ₁) ≥ n/(j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1}−1).

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, with area A when n = 2 and volume |Ω| in general, and let λ₁ ≤ λ₂ ≤ ··· be the Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues. Is the scale-invariant quantity |Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁ always at least the n-ball value C_n^{2/n} j_{p+1,1}², so that in particular A λ₃ ≥ (A λ₃)_disk = π j_{1,1}² in dimension 2?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² Aλ₃ ≥ (Aλ₃)|disk = πj²_{1,1}, and for Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ |Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λₙ₊₁)|n-ball = C_n^{2/n} j²_{p+1,1}.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let λ₂, …, λₙ₊₁ be the first nontrivial Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues after λ₁. Must the scale-invariant sum |Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁) be at least the corresponding n-ball value C_n^{2/n} n j_{p+1,1}²? In dimension 2, this is the conjecture A(λ₂ + λ₃) ≥ [A(λ₂ + λ₃)]_disk = 2π j_{1,1}².

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² A(λ₂ + λ₃) ≥ [A(λ₂ + λ₃)]|disk = 2πj²_{1,1}, and for Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ |Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁) ≥ [|Ω|^{2/n}(λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)]|n-ball = C_n^{2/n} n j²_{p+1,1}.

accepted.question_text: For Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues on bounded domains Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, do the next-level analogues of the Faber-Krahn-type inequalities hold—namely Aλ₅ ≥ (Aλ₅)_disk, A(λ₄+λ₅) ≥ [A(λ₄+λ₅)]_disk, |Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2} ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2})_{n-ball}, and |Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2}) ≥ the corresponding n-ball value? More generally, for each k ≥ 3, what is the optimal lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k, and which domain or limiting family of domains attains it?

evidence.quote: Analogous, but even more tenuous conjectures would be Aλ₅ ≥ (Aλ₅)|disk, A(λ₄ + λ₅) ≥ [A(λ₄ + λ₅)]|disk, |Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2} ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2})|n-ball, and |Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2}) ≥ [|Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})]|n-ball. Thus, in general it is an open problem to find the optimal lower bound to |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k for k ≥ 3 and to discover the shape of domain that saturates it.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let 0 = μ₀ < μ₁ ≤ μ₂ ≤ ··· be the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian, defined by −Δv = μv in Ω with ∂v/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω. Must the reciprocal sum |Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ) be at least the n-ball value n/(C_n^{2/n} p_{n/2,1}²), where p_{ν,1} is the first positive zero of the derivative of t^{1−ν}J_ν(t)? In dimension 2, this is the question whether (1/A)(1/μ₁ + 1/μ₂) ≥ [(1/A)(1/μ₁ + 1/μ₂)]_disk = 2/(π p_{1,1}²).

evidence.quote: Show that (36) holds for an arbitrary smooth bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝ², and, more generally, show |Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ) ≥ [|Ω|^{-2/n}(1/μ₁ + ··· + 1/μₙ)]|n-ball = n/(C_n^{2/n} p²_{n/2,1}).

accepted.question_text: If Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ is a bounded convex domain and 0 = μ₀ < μ₁ ≤ μ₂ ≤ ··· are the Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian on Ω, must the ratio μ₂/μ₁ always satisfy μ₂/μ₁ ≤ 4?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ and convex, show μ₂/μ₁ ≤ 4.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with n ≥ 4. For the clamped plate eigenvalue problem Δ²w = Γw in Ω with boundary conditions w = 0 and ∂w/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω, must the lowest eigenvalue Γ₁ satisfy the Faber-Krahn-type inequality |Ω|^{4/n} Γ₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{4/n} Γ₁)_{n-ball}?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ with n ≥ 4 prove that the lowest eigenvalue Γ₁ of (39)-(40) satisfies |Ω|^{4/n} Γ₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{4/n} Γ₁)|n-ball.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ with n ≥ 2. For the buckling problem Δ²v = −ΛΔv in Ω with v = 0 and ∂v/∂n = 0 on ∂Ω, must the lowest buckling eigenvalue Λ₁ satisfy the Faber-Krahn-type inequality |Ω|^{2/n} Λ₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} Λ₁)_{n-ball}?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ with n ≥ 2 prove that the lowest eigenvalue Λ₁ of (41)-(42) satisfies |Ω|^{2/n} Λ₁ ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} Λ₁)|n-ball.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ. Write λ₂(Ω), …, λₙ₊₁(Ω) for the second through (n+1)-st Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues of Ω, and Λ₁(Ω) for the lowest buckling eigenvalue. Is the stronger lower bound Λ₁(Ω) ≥ (1/n)(λ₂(Ω) + ··· + λₙ₊₁(Ω)) always true?

evidence.quote: It is interesting to note that if (45) could be improved to Λ₁(Ω) ≥ (1/n)(λ₂(Ω) + ··· + λₙ₊₁(Ω)), then this together with (26) (Problem 8 above) would prove (44).

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, let λ₁(Ω) be its first Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalue, and let Λ₁(Ω) be its first buckling eigenvalue. Must the scale-invariant product |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω) always be at least the n-ball value C_n^{4/n} j_{p,1}² j_{p+1,1}², where p = (n−2)/2?

evidence.quote: Another conjecture that suggests itself ... is |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω) ≥ [|Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)Λ₁(Ω)]|n-ball = C_n^{4/n} j²_{p,1} j²_{p+1,1}.

accepted.question_text: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ. What is the optimal lower bound for the scale-invariant product |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)λ₂(Ω), where λ₁ and λ₂ are the first two Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues? Likewise, if Ω is convex, what is the optimal lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ₂(Ω)?

evidence.quote: Other problems suggested by the line of development above would be to find the best lower bound for |Ω|^{4/n} λ₁(Ω)λ₂(Ω), or for |Ω|^{2/n} λ₂(Ω) when Ω is convex.

accepted.question_text: For the clamped plate eigenvalues Γ₁ ≤ Γ₂ ≤ ··· and the buckling eigenvalues Λ₁ ≤ Λ₂ ≤ ··· on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, is the ball the maximizer of the first nontrivial ratios Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁? More generally, what are the sharp upper bounds for ratios such as Γ_{m+1}/Γ_m, Λ_{m+1}/Λ_m, (Γ₂+Γ₃)/Γ₁, and (Λ₂+Λ₃)/Λ₁?

evidence.quote: One could also investigate combinations of eigenvalues of the clamped plate and buckling problems ... one should begin with the ratios Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁ ... but the natural conjectures that Γ₂/Γ₁ and Λ₂/Λ₁ should be maximized when Ω is an n-ball are as yet unproved.

accepted.question_text: Let λ_k and μ_k denote the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues of a bounded planar domain Ω of area A, with μ₀ = 0. Do Pólya’s conjectures hold, namely μ_k < 4πk/A < λ_k for every k = 1, 2, ...? More generally, are Dirichlet eigenvalues always above, and Neumann eigenvalues always below, their Weyl asymptotic values in all dimensions?

evidence.quote: Perhaps the most compelling of these are Pólya's conjectures for the Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian ... For n = 2, these statements are expressed concisely by μ_k < 4πk/A < λ_k for k = 1,2,....
